title: --no-resume leaves media stage outputs in place despite promising a full rerun

evidence.quote:
@click.option(
    "--no-resume",
    is_flag=True,
    default=False,
    help="Ignore cached stage outputs and rerun everything.",

for name in [
        f"video_info_{video_id}.json",
        f"transcript_{video_id}.json",
        f"screenshots_{video_id}.json",
        f"ocr_results_{video_id}.json",
        f"lots_{video_id}.json",
        f"metadata_{video_id}.json",
        f"result_{video_id}.json",
    ]:

reasoning: The CLI contract says `--no-resume` ignores cached stage outputs and reruns everything, but `_clear_cache` only removes JSON/checkpoint files and the screenshots directory. It leaves media artifacts such as audio sources, extracted WAVs, and OCR videos untouched, so a user trying to recover from a stale or corrupt media stage can still rerun against old stage outputs.
reproduction: Create a run directory containing `audio_<id>.wav`, `audio_source_<id>.m4a`, and `video_ocr_<id>_480p.mp4`, then invoke the CLI with `--no-resume`; `_clear_cache` does not remove those media files before the download stages run.
recommendation: Either extend `_clear_cache` to remove every stage artifact covered by the `--no-resume` contract, including audio source files, WAV files, and OCR videos for the selected video/resolution, or narrow the CLI help/docs to state that media downloads are intentionally retained.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests cover option validation, summary math, and batch reports, but no test exercises `_clear_cache` or asserts which artifacts `--no-resume` invalidates.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a focused test that seeds a run directory with all stage artifact names, calls `_clear_cache(run_dir, video_id)`, and asserts the files expected to be invalidated by `--no-resume` are removed.
minimumFixScope: `main.py` `_clear_cache` plus a focused unit test for cache invalidation semantics.
